findings.message: The result is saved only for failures after the claim. Returns that fail earlier save nothing: `denied` and `incomplete` from GitHub (callback.ts lines 14-16) and an `expired` or reused state (claimConnect throws before the `.catch` that saves the result). The screen then shows `latestResult`, which is the newest saved result from the last 10 minutes, whatever attempt it came from. So the note can describe an earlier attempt, not the one that just returned. It also means the `denied`, `incomplete` and `expired` wording in RESULTS can never be shown. Fix: save every result code the callback gives, including the ones from before the claim. For an expired or used state, save it on the row found by `state_hash` and `user_id`, or on a new row for that person. Or stop showing a saved result that is older than this return. Add test cases for denied, incomplete and expired, each one after an earlier saved result.
findings.scenario: At 10:00 Kasun's connect from link A fails with `no-email`, and that result is saved. Kasun adds a verified email on GitHub, then uses link A again (browser back). The callback's claim fails because the state was already used, so the URL says `?github=expired` and nothing is saved. The screen shows the 10:00 result: "GitHub has no verified email for you". The right message is "that link has expired or was already used". In the same way, if Kasun cancels on GitHub (`?github=denied`) after connecting successfully through another unused link, the screen shows "GitHub connected as @…".

findings.message: AC-5 says a signed-out return goes to sign-in and then back to the callback. The test only checks the redirect to /signin with a `next` that starts with the callback path. It never signs in, so it never checks that the browser lands back on the callback and then on /git-accounts. Sign in on that page and assert the final URL.
findings.scenario: If the sign-in page dropped or changed `next` (for example, localPath rejecting a path with a query), the person would end up on the home page and lose the connect, and this test would still pass.

findings.message: The note is supposed to show how this return from GitHub came out. It actually shows the newest result recorded for the person in the last 10 minutes. Only failures after `claimConnect` are recorded. A return that fails earlier writes nothing: `error=access_denied`, a query that doesn't parse, and an expired or already-used state, which is the 'expired' refusal thrown by `claimConnect` itself. In those cases the screen falls back to an earlier attempt's result, or to UNMATCHED, and the 'denied', 'incomplete' and 'expired' wording can never appear. Fix: record every outcome against the state the return carries. For example, look up the `connect_state` row by state hash and user, and record the denied, incomplete or expired result on it. Or carry the claim id in the redirect and read exactly that row, owned by the viewer.
findings.scenario: Kasun connects and the store refuses with 'all-taken', which is recorded. Kasun asks to connect again and clicks Cancel on GitHub, so the URL has `github=denied`. The screen says every email is linked to another person. In another order: a successful connect, then a cancelled reconnect within 10 minutes, and the screen reads 'GitHub connected as @…'.

findings.message: `findGitIdentity` puts a login match ahead of an email match. A commit whose login has been reused therefore resolves to the first holder's connected row. `isVerifiedEmailOf` then rejects the email, and `authorOf` returns null. It never goes on to the identity that the commit's email does belong to. This fix stops the wrong person being credited, but it also stops the right person being credited when they took the renamed login. Fix: when the connected row matched by login fails the email check, resolve by the commit email instead. That means the connected identity holding that verified email, or the legacy path. Add that case to the table test in `modules/delivery/tests/ingest-112.test.ts`.
findings.scenario: Kasun connected as `kasun-old` and later renamed his GitHub account. Nimal took the login `kasun-old` and connected GitHub with the verified email nimal@lumen.test. Nimal pushes a commit with login `kasun-old` and email nimal@lumen.test. `findGitIdentity` returns Kasun's row, the email check fails, and the commit is credited to nobody instead of to Nimal.
